messages.content: The sky is blue because of how sunlight scatters in our atmosphere. Air molecules are much better at scattering shorter wavelengths (blue light) than longer ones (red light), so when sunlight enters the atmosphere, blue light gets scattered in all directions while other colors mostly pass straight through. That's why you see blue when you look up at the sky from any angle.
